graph_meta.problem_text: Find the LCM and HCF of the following pairs of integers and verify that LCM × HCF = product of the two numbers. (i) 26 and 91 (ii) 510 and 92 (iii) 336 and 54
graph_meta.sympy_note: No unknown, so no equation. Factorisations are checked by the node's `factorise` list (every factor must be prime and the product right); other lines by SymPy's value checks.
graph_meta.guided_note: Guided mode: after the plan, the pairs in any order. '(ii)' or 'ii)' picks pair (ii); a line without a label is for the pair being solved. Per pair four questions (factorise, HCF, LCM, verify); a correct division or split of either number is working at the factorise question. Wrong answers: Hint 1, 2, then 3.
graph_meta.description: Guided solution DAG for NCERT Class 10 Ex 1.1 Q2: (i) HCF = 13, LCM = 182 (ii) HCF = 2, LCM = 23460 (iii) HCF = 6, LCM = 3024. For each pair: prime factorisation, HCF (shared primes, smallest powers), LCM (all primes, greatest powers), then LCM × HCF = product.

problem_context.source: NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 1 Real Numbers, Exercise 1.1, Q2 (p. 5)

glossary.definition: A prime factor is a factor that is also a prime number. For 10 = 2 × 5, the prime factors are 2 and 5.
A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. 2, 3, 5, 7, 11 and 13 are primes; 1 is not a prime.
A composite number has more than two factors, like 4, 6 or 9, so it can be broken into smaller factors.
A factor of a number divides it exactly. The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.
The HCF (highest common factor) is the largest number that divides both numbers exactly. HCF(8, 12) = 4.
The LCM (lowest common multiple) is the smallest number that both numbers divide into exactly. LCM(4, 6) = 12.
A multiple of a number is that number times a whole number. The multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, 16, …
A power is repeated multiplication: 3² = 3 × 3 and 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2.
The product is the answer to a multiplication: the product of 3 and 4 is 12.

nodes.label: Describe the Plan
nodes.description: Describe the plan: factorise both numbers; HCF = common primes, smallest powers; LCM = all primes, greatest powers; check LCM × HCF = product. Then the pairs (i) to (iii), in any order.
nodes.prompt: Describe your plan: how will you find the HCF and LCM of each pair, and verify LCM × HCF = product?
hints: Think about what HCF and LCM mean.
Both come from the prime factors of the two numbers.
Factorise, HCF from common primes, LCM from all primes, then check.

concepts_required.idea: writing both numbers as products of primes
hints: What do you need to know about the two numbers before you can find their HCF or LCM?
Break each number into its prime factors. Example: 12 = 2² × 3.
concepts_required.answer: Write both numbers as products of primes.

explain.question: Why do we factorise both numbers first?
explain.understanding: The HCF and the LCM are built from the primes of the two numbers, so we need to see those primes.

concepts_required.idea: HCF from the common primes at their smallest powers
hints: Once you have the primes, how do you get the HCF, the highest common factor?
The HCF can only use primes that are in both numbers. Which power of each: the smaller or the bigger?
concepts_required.answer: HCF = product of the common primes, each to its smallest power.

explain.question: Why does the HCF use only the common primes?
explain.understanding: The HCF must divide both numbers, so it can only contain primes, and powers, that both numbers have.

concepts_required.idea: LCM from all the primes at their greatest powers
hints: And how do you get the LCM, the lowest common multiple?
The LCM must be a multiple of both numbers. Which primes must it include, and to which power?
concepts_required.answer: LCM = product of every prime in either number, each to its greatest power.

explain.question: Why does the LCM use every prime at its greatest power?
explain.understanding: The LCM must be divisible by both numbers, so it needs every prime of each, at the biggest power.

concepts_required.idea: checking LCM × HCF = the product of the two numbers
hints: The question also asks you to verify something. What?
Work out LCM × HCF and the product of the two numbers. What should you find?
concepts_required.answer: Check that LCM × HCF equals the product of the two numbers.

explain.question: Why is it worth checking LCM × HCF = product?
explain.understanding: It is a quick check: if the two products differ, the HCF or the LCM is wrong.

misconceptions.response: Careful: the HCF uses only the primes both numbers share, and the LCM uses every prime from either number. Which goes with which?
HCF and LCM come from multiplying primes, not from adding the numbers. What do you need to know about each number first?

nodes.label: (i) Factorise 26 and 91
nodes.prompt: (i) Write 26 and 91 as products of prime factors.
hints: Factorise each number on its own. Example: 15 = 3 × 5.
Worked example: 22 = 2 × 11 and 35 = 5 × 7. For an odd number, test 3, 5, 7, … in order.

nodes.label: (i) HCF of 26 and 91
nodes.prompt: (i) What is the HCF of 26 and 91?
hints: The HCF multiplies the primes both numbers share, each to its smallest power.
Example: 10 = 2 × 5 and 35 = 5 × 7 share only 5, so HCF(10, 35) = 5.
HCF = 13

nodes.label: (i) LCM of 26 and 91
nodes.prompt: (i) What is the LCM of 26 and 91?
hints: The LCM takes every prime in either number, each to its greatest power.
Example: 10 = 2 × 5 and 35 = 5 × 7. All the primes: 2, 5, 7, so LCM(10, 35) = 70.

nodes.label: (i) Check LCM × HCF
nodes.prompt: (i) Verify: work out LCM × HCF and 26 × 91. Are they equal?
hints: Multiply your LCM by your HCF, then multiply the two numbers. Compare.
Example: for 10 and 35, LCM × HCF = 70 × 5 = 350 and 10 × 35 = 350. Do the same for your pair.
182 × 13 = 2366 and 26 × 91 = 2366, so LCM × HCF = product of the two numbers.

nodes.label: (ii) LCM of 510 and 92
nodes.prompt: (ii) What is the LCM of 510 and 92?
hints: The LCM takes every prime in either number, each to its greatest power.
Example: 8 = 2³ and 12 = 2² × 3. The greatest powers are 2³ and 3, so LCM(8, 12) = 24.

nodes.label: (ii) Check LCM × HCF

hints: Multiply your LCM by your HCF, then multiply the two numbers. Compare.
Example: for 8 and 12, LCM × HCF = 24 × 4 = 96 and 8 × 12 = 96. Do the same for your pair.
23460 × 2 = 46920 and 510 × 92 = 46920, so LCM × HCF = product of the two numbers.

nodes.label: (iii) Check LCM × HCF

hints: Multiply your LCM by your HCF, then multiply the two numbers. Compare.
Example: for 20 and 30, LCM × HCF = 60 × 10 = 600 and 20 × 30 = 600. Do the same for your pair.
3024 × 6 = 18144 and 336 × 54 = 18144, so LCM × HCF = product of the two numbers.
